summary: TiN thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with TiCl4 and NH3 as precursors. The films exhibited excellent step coverage, low resistivity, and low Cl impurity content. The process allows for precise control of film thickness and is suitable for complex substrates.
evidence: The physical properties including the step coverage of the TiN films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) technique, using TiCl4 and NH3 as the precursors have been investigated. The deposition rate of the TiN film is constant and moderately high (240.6 A° per cycle) under an optimum deposition condition. The film resistivity is appreciably low (24200 mO cm). The XRD analysis results indicate polycrystalline nature of the TiN films with a (1 1 1) preferred orientation. The XPS and AES analysis results establish that the Cl impurity concentration in the TiN films is lower than 1 at.%. The RMS surface roughness is low. Also it is found by SEM observation that the step coverage of the TiN films with trenches (the aspect ratio being 10:1) is excellent. One hundred percent conformality is observed for both the side/bottom and the side/top sections.
